name: Knit in the round
blurb: Circular knitting gets you hats, socks and sleeves — tubes with no seams. It also removes purling from stocking stitch entirely, which most people find a relief.
gear: A short circular needle, plus double-pointed needles or a long circular for the crown
steps: Knit a gauge swatch and actually measure it. In flat knitting you can fudge it; in a fitted hat you cannot.
Cast on, then join in the round — carefully, making sure the stitches are not twisted around the needle, which is unfixable later.
Place a marker at the start of the round so you always know where you are.
Knit a ribbed brim, then the body in stocking stitch, which in the round is just knitting forever.
Learn decreases (k2tog and ssk) for the crown, switching to double-pointed needles or magic loop as the circumference shrinks.
Thread the yarn through the last stitches, pull tight, and weave in the ends.
tips: A twisted join means starting completely over. Check twice before joining.
Ladders — loose columns where needles meet — are fixed by giving the first two stitches of each needle an extra tug.
proof: A hat that fits the intended head, with a neat crown and no ladders.
